To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ROMANIS, a second-generation ANI camera, was developed and demonstrated in the field, 2) ROMANIS recordings can be well modeled by a SαS distribution, and 3) ANI algorithms based fractiles and low-order moments of SalphaS distribution are developed and demonstrated.

(1) ambient noise in shallow waters can be modeled by an SαS distribution, and (2) ANI algorithms based only on low-order moments are sufficient to produce robust ANI images, and range estimation to an object is possible by passively identifying echoes from the object.

(i) the high frequency ambient noise is well described by a symmetric αstable distribution; (ii) ANI algorithms can be designed using fractiles of the SαS distribution; and (iii) the range to an object can be passivley estimated by analyzing the echoes from snaps.
